Looking at this problem, I need to determine whether a section of a vector bundle over a scheme is a closed embedding when the projection is separated.

**Answer: The statement is TRUE.**

**Proof.**

Let $\pi: V \to X$ be a vector bundle over a scheme $X$, and let $s: X \to V$ be a section, so $\pi \circ s = \mathrm{id}_X$. Assume $\pi$ is separated.

**Key fact:** A section of any separated morphism is a closed immersion. The separatedness of $\pi$ means the diagonal $\Delta_\pi: V \to V \times_X V$ is a closed immersion.

**Construction.** Define the morphism
$$f = (s \circ \pi,\; \mathrm{id}_V): V \to V \times_X V.$$
This is well-defined because both components map to $X$ compatibly:
$$\pi \circ (s \circ \pi) = (\pi \circ s) \circ \pi = \mathrm{id}_X \circ \pi = \pi = \pi \circ \mathrm{id}_V.$$

**Form the pullback square:**
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
Z & \xrightarrow{g} & V \\
\downarrow{h} & & \downarrow{\Delta_\pi} \\
V & \xrightarrow{f} & V \times_X V
\end{array}$$

**Compute the fiber product.** A point $(a, b) \in V \times V$ lies in $Z$ if and only if $\Delta_\pi(a) = f(b)$, i.e.,
$$(a, a) = (s(\pi(b)),\; b).$$
This gives $a = s(\pi(b))$ and $a = b$, hence $b = s(\pi(b))$. Therefore
$$Z = \{(b, b) \in V \times V : b = s(\pi(b))\} \cong \{b \in V : b \in \mathrm{im}(s)\}.$$

**Identify $Z$ with $X$.** The map $\pi|_{\mathrm{im}(s)}: \mathrm{im}(s) \to X$ is an isomorphism with inverse $s$ (since $\pi \circ s = \mathrm{id}_X$ and $s \circ \pi|_{\mathrm{im}(s)} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{im}(s)}$). Under the identification $Z \cong X$ via $b \mapsto \pi(b)$, the map $g: Z \to V$ becomes exactly $s: X \to V$.

**Conclusion.** Since $\Delta_\pi$ is a closed immersion (by separatedness of $\pi$) and closed immersions are stable under base change, the map $g: Z \to V$ is a closed immersion. But $g = s$ under the identification $Z \cong X$. Therefore $s: X \to V$ is a closed immersion. $\blacksquare$

**Remark.** The projection of a vector bundle is always an affine morphism (it is $\mathbf{Spec}$ of the symmetric algebra of a locally free sheaf), hence always separated. So the hypothesis "if the projection is a separated morphism" is automatically satisfied for any vector bundle. The substantive content is the general principle: *every section of a separated morphism is a closed immersion*, proved above by exhibiting the section as a base change of the diagonal.
